kind: DR02 bounded static research inventory, not canon or runtime certification
selection: Four world records (Firstsun, Yolen, Dhatri, Emberdark) and all 10 nested sites; e61/e62; codex entries matching Dusk, Starling, Autonomy, Perpendicularities (3 matches in PR24/48; 4 in PR37); Lumar era12; h-dusk with both pairs; Cognitive Realm overview. This is a bounded selection, not every DR02 claim in the atlas.

worlds.name: First of the Sun
worlds.blurb: An ocean world with one large mainland and many islands where the Eelakin live. The greatest island, Patji, is a jungle where almost everything can kill you. Trappers like Dusk survive by knowing its rules and by the Aviar, birds that give their owners talents such as seeing danger coming. Now ships from the Ones Above have arrived in orbit. On this globe the Pantheon islands are drawn about five times larger, and the homeisles three times, so they can be seen.
worlds.short: Patji and the Aviar: Sixth of the Dusk.

12.blurb: An ocean world of islands. The greatest, Patji, is a deadly jungle where the Aviar live, and Patji itself is an avatar of Autonomy. Years after the Ones Above appeared, Dusk sees his people racing to modernise before they are conquered, and he sails through Patji’s Eye into the Emberdark to find help.

cognitive.name: Drominad’s subastral
cognitive.blurb: Much like the unsea: black, coral-like ground and a few small islands, blue smoke-like streaks across the sky, no visible sun, and people and Aviar shown as floating, fishhook-shaped lights.

sites.name: Patji
sites.desc: The Father island, the largest of the Pantheon: wedge-shaped, with knife-edged peaks and a jungle that punishes every mistake. Aviar must visit it to gain their talents. Dusk traps here.

sites.name: Patji’s Eye
sites.desc: A green-tinted lake of not-quite-water in a canyon toward Patji’s eastern peak, holding glowing worms. It is a perpendicularity, and Dusk sails through it into the Emberdark.

sites.name: The Northern Interests fort
sites.desc: A fortified wooden stronghold with cannons at the far end of Patji, where the Ones Above set their machine.

sites.name: Sori
sites.desc: The smallest and tamest island of the Pantheon, closest to home, where young trappers train.

sites.name: The Homeisles
sites.desc: The tamed islands of the Eelakin, with their cities and reefs, about three weeks’ rowing from the Pantheon. Their layout here is our placeholder.

sites.name: The mainland
sites.desc: A frozen wasteland to the south of the homeisles, with native ravens and no sign of people.

worlds.name: Yolen
worlds.blurb: The world where it all began. Humans, dragons and the strange Sho Del all came from Yolen, and it was here, long before any of the books, that a group of conspirators shattered Adonalsium into sixteen Shards. Khriss writes that it is shrouded and hidden somewhere in the cosmere. The books have barely shown the planet itself; this surface is an interpretation.
worlds.short: Origin of humanity and of the Shattering.
facts: Hidden; not on the star chart

12.blurb: The world where it all began. Humans, dragons and the Sho Del all came from Yolen, and it was here that Adonalsium was shattered into sixteen Shards. It is hidden from most of the cosmere. In Isles of the Emberdark, Starling, a young dragon living in human form, was exiled from Yolen twelve years before the story. The planet itself is still barely described; this surface is an interpretation.

sites.name: The greatstar
sites.desc: A glowing hole high in Yolen’s atmosphere where the Silverlight Nexus comes through, with a flying city of dragons nearby. Its position on the globe is our placeholder.

sites.name: Fainlife lands
sites.desc: Regions overrun by bone-white invasive life; about half the trees are white.

sites.name: The Shattering (site unknown)
sites.desc: Somewhere on Yolen, eighteen conspirators struck down Adonalsium with a weapon made from the Dawnshards. The exact place has never been shown.

worlds.name: Dhatri
worlds.blurb: Named in Isles of the Emberdark: the homeworld of the Aethers and the centre of the Dhatrian planetary network, which includes Lumar. It has lost its perpendicularity but has starships. This surface is a placeholder.
facts: The Lost Metal and Isles of the Emberdark

worlds.status: A region of the Cognitive Realm
worlds.blurb: A dark region of the Cognitive Realm that Dusk enters through Patji’s Eye. Here he meets Starling, a young dragon serving on a starship, who has found a map to a hidden gate back into the physical world.

sites.name: The hidden gate
sites.desc: The way back to the physical world shown on Starling’s old map.

codex.desc: Places where a Shard’s power touches all three Realms, used as gates between worlds. Patji’s Eye is one.

cognitive_realm.title: The Cognitive Realm
cognitive_realm.text: The realm of thought, laid over the same space. It is one flat plane on which each world appears as a flattened reflection, its subastral, shaped by what its people think. On most worlds the solid and the fluid swap places: Roshar’s land becomes an ocean of glass beads and its seas become dark ground. The sky is black, with no stars or moon, and living minds show as lights. Space that nobody thinks about collapses, so worlds light-years apart are days or weeks apart here, which is why they are drawn much closer together. Between the subastrals lies the emberdark, a starless black void with a transparent, liquid-like surface called the unsea. The two realms only line up exactly at perpendicularities.
cognitive_realm.unknown: The books have not described this world’s subastral. It is drawn with the common pattern: solid and fluid swapped, under a black sky.
